messages:
Maya (Security): Heads up — AcmeCorp's security questionnaire just listed two asks: evidence of KMS key rotation/escrow policy and correlation between RBAC role changes and audit log entries. They want proof for Dedicated/on-prem. Can we prep?
Lucas - Solutions: pinging @Aj Patel + @Samir — they were on the Dedicated runtime infra.
Aj Patel: saw that. main questions: are we proving that tenant keys are rotated monthly? Also they asked about key import/export controls for HSMs.
Samir: For Dedicated on-prem we recommend customer-managed HSM. We have rotation metadata in the KMS audit logs but need to show exported key history is disabled. I'll pull logs.
Frances Chen: Also note they asked for RBAC changeproof — need who changed role, which API call, and matching audit log id. We have SIEM events that correlate to IAM write calls and request_id.
Maya (Security): If possible produce a short playbook + 3 artifacts: (1) rotation schedule + a sample key rotation entry, (2) audit query that shows role change -> user mapping, (3) a short statement about key import disabled for the managed control plane. Customer prefers CSV evidence.
Aj Patel: I can run these queries. sample audit query I use for rotation export: 
```
index=redwood-audit event_type=key_rotation tenant_id=acmecorp | table ts, key_id, actor, rotation_type, request_id
```
Will export to CSV and redact identifiers as needed.
Samir: For role changes, use: 
```
index=redwood-audit action=role.update | where target_tenant=acmecorp | table ts, actor, role_before, role_after, request_id
```
Include request_id to tie back to traces and to the console change event.
Lucas - Solutions: We should prepare a short paragraph on KMS import policy: 'Dedicated customers may bring keys to customer HSMs; Redwood control plane does not persist unencrypted key material and import/export operations are disabled by default for hosted keys.' Can Legal sign off? @Frances Chen maybe.
Frances Chen: I'll draft language, but legal needs to review. Also add an incident-response blurb: if a vuln is found affecting KMS API integrity we'll notify within 24h and provide IOCs and remediation timeline. Draft: 'Security incidents impacting key material or KMS API call integrity are escalated to customers within 24 hours with remediation steps and audit artifacts.'
SecBot: Incident INC-2026-009 created by Samir — vuln triage queued.
Maya (Security): FYI we found a minor vuln in the gRPC auth handshake on a Dedicated patch; Samir is triaging. Need timeline for fixes and a customer-facing statement.
Samir: Triage suggests a patch in ~48 hours. Immediate mitigations: (1) apply ACL rules to block anomalous peers, (2) rotate affected keys (planned), (3) enable stricter request signing on the runtime. I'll produce the rotation proof after patch.
Aj Patel: I'll export the CSVs (rotation entries + role-change rows) and upload to secure-share. Tagging customer with redacted PII and including request_id mapping. :thumbsup:
Lucas - Solutions: Also prep an FAQ for the call: common Qs (key custody, rotation cadence, on-prem HSMs, audit log retention and SIEM export). I'll draft.
Maya (Security): Can we do a 30-min pre-call tomorrow 10:00am PT to rehearse? Want to run artifacts and Q&A.
Samir: 10:00am PT works for me. I'll have the triage notes + mitigation steps ready.
Frances Chen: I'll get Legal to review the KMS import/export paragraph and confirm wording by EOD.
Aj Patel: Uploading provisional CSVs now to secure-share/redwood/acmecorp (will remove tenant ids).
Maya (Security): Great, thanks team. After pre-call we'll finalize the short evidence packet (CSV + one-page playbook + legal blurb).
Lucas - Solutions: Noted — I'll take the customer-facing slides.
Aj Patel: :eyes:
Samir: filing postmortem template items in the incident ticket once patch is out.
Maya (Security): Keeping thread here for artifacts and final sign-off.
